title: Power / Design: read the simulator and its limitations
description: Understand the actual planning controls, simulated detection curves and warnings without mistaking a small demonstration or contradictory headline for validated design advice.
objectives: Distinguish simulation assumptions from acquired experimental data.
Read usable fits, detection fractions and uncertainty correctly.
Recognize the same-design recommendation error and preserve the recorded evidence.
prerequisite: This is a critical review of the actual recorded simulator, not calibrated statistical power or sample-size advice. Power_recorded_simulation_review.zip preserves the original JSON and an explanatory review; it is not a GUI-importable completed run or a native export demonstration. The recorded spaCR 1.5.0.4 screen, design adapter, simulator and fitting code still match current source bytes. Two marginal scans produced 18 fits and nine points, two replicates per point; four nonconverged fits remain in the denominator. Two simulations clipped probabilities. The same nominal baseline has different random draws: 1/2 versus 2/2 detections. The advice to increase to the existing well count is explicitly rejected and remains unfixed. Some plot endpoint labels are clipped; the verified table contains all nine coordinates. No new simulation, acquired data, biological calibration, GPU task, AI-provider request or publication is claimed. API: spacr.qt.widgets.power_design.DesignSpec/simulator_kwargs/power_curve and spacr.qt.screens.power.run_power_sweep; spacr.power_simulate and spacr.power_model perform simulation and fitting.

scenes.narration: Power and Design explores assumptions with simulated data. It does not load an acquired experiment or establish that its assumptions match yours. This lesson reads a real recorded run, including its warnings and a misleading recommendation. Do not use this small demonstration as validated sample-size advice.

Start with the library and scoring unit. Switching between guide and gene changes what the model scores: the displayed example has forty genes and four guides per gene, so guide scoring has one hundred sixty units. Gene scoring pools the guide information. These are teaching assumptions, not new biological measurements.

The plate and effect controls describe the assumed design. A positive-call rate is a simulated classification probability, not a count of organisms or a measured infection rate. Inspect the background, effect and prevalence together, and remember that the displayed assumptions do not validate the model.

An effect below one triggers the native unsupported-direction warning and disables Run. The recording then restores a supported value so the controls recover. This is a software guard, not a claim that effects in the other direction are biologically impossible. Do not bypass the warning to obtain a convenient curve.

This bounded demonstration uses only two replicates per point. The detection rule is a usable fit reaching the chosen area under the receiver operating characteristic curve threshold. It is not a hypothesis-test P-value cutoff. The seed and backend are recorded; selecting Torch alone does not prove GPU execution.

Run starts the actual threaded simulator. It varies the cell-count and well-count axes separately, rather than evaluating every combination. The recording completed eighteen fits across nine points. Keep the settings and raw replicate records together so a plotted fraction can be traced to the fits that produced it.

Read detections as counts over all requested replicates. Four fits did not converge and remain in the denominator as non-detections; they are not silently discarded. A plotted hundred percent here means only two out of two. Such a small sample cannot establish a precise detection probability.

The table separates detection fractions from mean performance among usable fits. An unavailable mean is not zero. Average precision also needs its prevalence baseline for context. Read the table when a plot-end label is clipped, and inspect nonconvergence counts instead of judging the design from the blue line alone.

The headline contains an error. Both baseline estimates already use ninety-six wells, but different random draws produce one of two detections in one scan and two of two in the other. Going to the same ninety-six wells is not an improvement in design. Reject that recommendation; this tutorial does not repair it.

Expand the remaining caveats. Two simulated screens clipped probabilities above one, so their realised occupancy differs from the requested value. The model has other assumptions and limitations; listing them is not validation. Review these warnings and the failed fits before drawing conclusions from any simulation.

The linked archive preserves the actual recorded specification, replicate outputs, curves, table and incorrect headline for inspection. It is an external evidence download, not a native GUI export or an imported result. The Python design adapter and simulation APIs expose the same workflow, but real planning requires separate validation of assumptions and uncertainty.
